root_cause_label: Repeated use of inappropriate solvers and custom gradient descent for high-dimensional constrained optimization, combined with no task completion signal
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose computationally intractable solvers (SLSQP, trust-constr, COBYLA) for a 1000-variable constrained problem and then spent the tail of the trajectory on a naive custom gradient descent that yielded a suboptimal solution, never calling finish to submit the result.
t_err_evidence: At step 7 the agent launches scipy SLSQP on a 1000-variable constrained problem, which is computationally prohibitive and will not converge in reasonable time; a proper approach (e.g., cvxpy with a QP-capable solver) was available and not considered.
t_commit_evidence: At step 20 the agent abandons all standard solvers and rewrites the script as a custom projected gradient descent, locking the trajectory into an approach that cannot match oracle-quality results and from which it never recovers.
t_surface_evidence: At step 11 the L-BFGS-B run reports 'Optimization successful: False' with sum=126 (constraint violated) and a very high cost of 135.7, making the failure of the chosen approach observable.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge that SLSQP (and subsequently L-BFGS-B, trust-constr, COBYLA) are impractical for a 1000-variable constrained convex program, and does not recognise that cvxpy with a dedicated QP/convex solver would be the correct tool.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 8-9 produce empty output as SLSQP hangs indefinitely; the agent then interrupts (step 10) and repeats a structurally similar solver (L-BFGS-B at step 11) that also fails, and the SLSQP pattern is repeated again at steps 17-19 and COBYLA at steps 25-27.
